newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates steady on exporters' demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates steady on exporters' demand.

text.p: Pakistan cotton rates remained steady on Monday on demand from exporters and dealers said prices would rise on fears that recent rains could delay the arrival of the new 1997/98 (July-June) crop.

"Prices are likely to rise because good quality stocks are limited," dealer Nasim Usman said. "Delay in the arrival of the new crop would further push up rates as there is demand from exporters and mill owners."
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 was traded at around 1,950 rupees ($48.16) per maund (37.32 k.g.) and K-68 at 2,200 rupees, dealers said.
